To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

life support systems have been developed for failing essential organs, that they can prolong life but do not always do so, that their ethical implications are complex, that their cost/benefit ratios vary widely, and that they are used most rationally when the physician is aware of all the relevant facts, including the cost/benefit ratios.
life support systems are an important tool in intensive care, but their use should be restricted to the most severely ill patients.
